title: API failure incident synthesis and responder cheat sheet (draft)
content:
Status: draft — quick reference for on-call responders. Use this as a short, pragmatic checklist + synthesis for common API failures (client-visible timeouts, 429s / quota throttles, degraded streaming, and sudden elevated error rates).

Purpose and scope:
- Provide a single-page quick triage + recovery recipe for first responders.
- Not exhaustive; links to long-form runbooks and postmortem templates at the bottom.
- Intended for SREs on pager and platform engineers doing fast mitigation.

TL;DR first 5 minutes (do these in order):
1) Confirm the symptom and blast radius: which endpoint(s) / route(s)? examples: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings, /v1/stream. Check dashboards (Grafana) and ops-alert channel.
2) Determine scope: is it single-region, multi-region, single model, or global? Look at routing logs (edge-router and model-router).
3) If user impact clear, flip SEV to match impact and notify (Slack #sre oncall + #platform) and add incident in INC tracker.
4) Apply quick containment if safe: route traffic to fallback model variant or scale dedicated pool (follow safe-ops checklist below).
5) Keep a running incident note: start a short lived Google Doc or use the incident channel thread as the canonical timeline.

Quick signals to check (fast):
- Grafana: 500/502/503 spikes, 429 rate, p50/p95/p99 latency for affected routes, stream reconnect counts.
- Router logs: 5xx by upstream (runtime vs model-serving).
- Model runtime health: GPU task queue depth, backlog, OOMs, kernel crashes.
- Edge vs internal: Are requests failing at edge LB or after routing to runtime?
- Token/time budgets: burst limits or quota manager hit (429s).

Common failure categories and immediate actions:

A) Client-visible timeouts (API returns timeout / gateway timeouts)
- Likely causes: long model generation, runaway prompt, KV cache thrash, overloaded GPUs, runtime GC.
- Quick checks: active request queue lengths (Serving Runtime dashboard), per-model avg seq length change, recent model rollout or commit.
- Mitigations (fast):
  * If model-specific: fail over to a lighter model variant (route /v1/generate -> model x-quantized) using the routing console (rollout -> instant route override).
  * If region-specific: shift traffic to healthy region (edge routing policy -> region failover).
  * If overload: increase worker replicas temporarily (scale pool command in console) but prefer fallback routing to avoid spin-up delays.
  * If request-level: enforce a shorter request-level timeout at gateway (gateway config -> shorter client timeout) to reduce resource hogging.
- When NOT to scale: if GPU memory OOMs or kernel crashes are suspected — scaling will exacerbate.

B) Elevated 429s (throttling / quota)
- Likely causes: legitimate spike, buggy client retry loop, quota misconfiguration, rate-limiter regression.
- Quick checks: rate limiter logs, quota counters in Redis, recent deploy touching limiter config, spike in repeat requests from small set of IPs.
- Mitigations (fast):
  * If legitimate spike from high-value customer, apply temporary quota bump via console (increase quota for org).
  * If runaway client, block/put IPs in short banlist at edge (edge-allowlist/blocklist).
  * If buggy retries, enable short-term global token bucket relaxation (lower strictness) for 1–10 minutes.
  * Notify product/support for customer-impacting adjustments.
- Note: any permanent quota change must go through billing/eng review.

C) Degraded streaming (partial frames, reconnects, slow stream)
- Likely causes: broken keepalive, proxy buffering changes, backpressure misconfig, runtime streaming bug, or network flaps between edge and runtime.
- Quick checks: stream reconnect rates, TCP connection resets, env-lib proxy logs (nginx/Envoy), client-side error patterns.
- Mitigations (fast):
  * Toggle streaming muxer to legacy code-path (console feature flags) if a recent deploy touched streaming.
  * Short circuit to non-streaming endpoint as fallback (ask app teams: is chunked streaming required?).
  * If proxy is buffering, change proxy config to disable buffering for affected route and reload proxy on a single host for testing.
  * Roll back recent streaming-related deploys (use canary rollback in console).
- Temporary workaround: return short-circuit summary responses (e.g., complete generation server-side) for clients that can accept it.

D) Elevated error rates (5xx spikes with no clear 1 cause)
- Likely causes: infra regression, host OS kernel issue, dependency outage (e.g., metrics DB or KMS), or bad model binary.
- Quick checks: correlate errors with deploys (GitHub PR timestamps), infra alerts (host-level CPU/IO), dependency health pages.
- Mitigations (fast):
  * If recent deploy present: rollback that deploy using the release engineering rollback recipe.
  * If dependency outage: fail open to degraded mode (e.g., skip expensive evals, use cached responses).
  * If host-level issue: cordon and drain affected hosts and shift traffic to healthy hosts.
  * If unknown: enable detailed debug logging for a narrow time window and sample traffic (keep logs for min 48h).

Safe-ops checklist (do before making global changes):
- Announce in #sre-oncall and incident channel what you're about to change (scale/fallback/route override).
- Smallest blast radius first: test change on canary / single region.
- If applying routing override, keep a 10–15 min watch window with active monitoring.
- Document all manual changes in the incident timeline doc with timestamps and owner.

Tools and useful commands (examples):
- Check router logs (last 15m): kubectl -n prod logs deploy/router --since=15m | grep "/v1/generate"
- Check queue depth: curl -sS http://runtime-metrics.internal/queues | jq .
- Route override (console/CLI): infra-cli route override --route /v1/generate --to model:fast-4bit --reason "incident containment"
- Scale pool: infra-cli pools scale --name dedicated-gpu-pool-3 --replicas 12 --reason incident
- Block IPs at edge: edge-cli block add --ip 1.2.3.4 --ttl 600 --reason suspicious-retries
- Rollback last canary: release-cli rollback --deployment runtime-streaming --to-version v2025-02-07

Escalation matrix (quick):
- 0–15m: oncall SRE (owner) manages containment actions.
- 15–45m: senior SRE + platform eng on call (if mitigation requires infra changes).
- 45m+: paging lead and maybe on-call PM if customer-impacting > 1 hour.

Post-incident quick wrap (first 24h):
- Capture mitigating actions, why chosen, and evidence of recovery.
- Assign a postmortem owner within 24 hours (usually oncall owner).
- Temp follow-ups: revert any quick, broad relaxations (rate limits, quotas) unless approved.
- If rollback used, schedule root-cause analysis before rolling forward.

Notes to self / open questions (work-in-progress):
- Add small flow diagram for stream vs non-stream fallback decisions.
- Automate safe route override for model fallback with automatic revert after 10m if no error improvement.
- Consider making the token-bucket relaxation for 429s a single button in console (guarded by approvals).
- Validate runbook commands across staging clusters (some CLI flags differ).

Related long-form docs:
- Confluence: API Operations Home (see linked artifacts)
- Long-form runbooks: "runtime-api-stability-first-aid" and "failure-modes-rapid-fallbacks" (linked in the SRE space)

TODOs for this doc:
- Convert the quick commands into verified scripts in infra/tools.
- Add contact roster with phone numbers for 3rd-party support (CDN, cloud provider).
- Get review from product-hosted-api and serving-runtime leads.

If you pick this up as responder: ping me (Lena) in #sre-oncall for context and I will add the incident note skeleton.

-- end of cheat-sheet (draft)
